title: Paint Bucket
statement: A drawing app stores a picture as a grid of colour numbers. The paint bucket tool, used on cell (row, col) with a new colour, repaints that cell and every cell connected to it up, down, left or right through cells of the same original colour. Return the picture after one use of the tool.

answerKey.pattern: Flood fill: BFS or DFS on a grid
keyPoints: Remember the starting cell's original colour
If it already equals the new colour, return the picture unchanged
Visit the four neighbours of each repainted cell, staying inside the grid
Only spread into cells of the original colour; repainting marks them as visited
edgeCases: New colour equals the old colour (otherwise an endless loop)
acceptableSlowerApproaches: Repeatedly sweep the whole grid, repainting cells next to repainted ones until nothing changes: O((R · C)²)

hints: Each cell is a vertex, and its up, down, left and right neighbours of the same colour are its edges.
Start a search at (row, col). Which cells may the paint spread into?
Store the old colour first. If it equals the new colour, stop at once; otherwise the repainted colour itself marks visited cells.
